ai.title: Add host platform override to SDK run options
ai.summary: The SDK now supports a `hostPlatform` option that overrides the reported operating system for a run. This allows hosted runners to report the user's local environment (e.g., `win32` on a Linux server) so the model generates commands compatible with the user's shell and filesystem. The new `applyHostPlatform` function is called during `runOnce` and updates the session's `systemInfo.platform`, while leaving the `shell` configuration unaffected.

facts: The reset's fallback write is best-effort: on a terminal that is gone the stream reports EIO a tick later, which with no listener is an uncaught exception. We are exiting; there is nothing to do about it.

The terminal went away (window closed, SSH dropped): a write or read on it fails. Not a crash. Mid-exit, let the exit already running finish; otherwise leave as a closed window does, keeping the hour for resume.
A file error carries its path (`EIO: i/o error, write '/path'`); a terminal stream's does not, so only a bare read or write counts.
Best-effort immediate reset. Keep the watchdog armed below so it can retry after this process exits if the buffered write is lost.
entries.title: CLI update: renderer-cleanup

ai.title: Treat closed terminal write errors as clean exit in CLI
ai.summary: The CLI no longer records a fatal crash when a write or read fails with EIO, ENXIO, or EPIPE on the controlling terminal, which accounts for about 95% of `cli.fatal_crash` events as of 2026-11-21. A new `isTerminalGoneError` function in `cli/src/utils/terminal-gone.ts` distinguishes terminal loss from actual file errors by checking that the error has no `path` property and matches the specific syscall codes. In `cli/src/utils/renderer-cleanup.ts`, the `uncaughtException` and `unhandledRejection` handlers now call `handleExternalExit` for these errors, allowing the process to exit gracefully while preserving the Freebuff session for resume rather than terminating with a fatal error report.
ai.evidence: New file `cli/src/utils/terminal-gone.ts` defines `isTerminalGoneError` to classify EIO, ENXIO, and EPIPE errors on bare reads or writes as terminal loss rather than crashes; `cli/src/utils/renderer-cleanup.ts` imports this utility and uses it in `uncaughtException` and `unhandledRejection` handlers to trigger `handleExternalExit` instead of `exitCliWithFatalError`.

eli5.text: Closing your terminal window or dropping your remote connection no longer registers as a crash for the Freebuff assistant in your terminal. The software now recognizes that the screen has simply disappeared, rather than the program failing. This keeps any active session intact so you can pick up where you left off next time you open it, instead of losing your progress and being billed again for a new session.

ai.title: MCP tool listing follows pages, and Next preparation finds packages
ai.summary: In `common/src/mcp/client.ts`, `listMCPTools` now delegates to `listAllTools`, which pages through a server's `tools/list` results via `nextCursor` until `MCP_LIST_TOOLS_MAX` tools or `MCP_LIST_TOOLS_MAX_PAGES` are reached, and evicts a rejected promise from `listToolsCache` so a slow or flaky server can be retried on the next call. The same change adds `common/src/mcp/list-tools.ts` exporting `listAllMcpTools`, `MCP_LIST_TOOLS_MAX`, `MCP_LIST_TOOLS_MAX_PAGES`, and `McpToolsPage`. In `common/src/sites/next-prepare.ts`, the embedded preparation program replaces `createRequire` resolution with a manual `node_modules` walk, because Node 20/24/26 cache a failed `package.json` lookup for the rest of the process, which made first-time builds fail after installing the adapter.

Separately, `common/src/sites/next-prepare.ts` rewrites `packageRoot` to walk `node_modules` directly instead of using `projectRequire.resolve`, and adds `error?.stack` to the `PREPARATION failed` log write.

eli5.text: The assistant can now find every tool offered by an external helper program, even if the helper lists them in batches, so you see the complete set of capabilities instead of just the first few. In the same update, the setup for publishing web apps now locates the necessary files by checking the folder directly, which prevents the first attempt at building a new site from crashing due to a remembered error from before the files were installed.
